LDL tells you how much cholesterol the particles carry. ApoB counts the particles.

Every particle that can slip into an artery wall and build plaque carries one ApoB. Canadian guidelines (CCS 2021) prefer ApoB or non-HDL cholesterol when triglycerides are above 1.5 mmol/L.

ApoB and Lp(a) are both part of our longevity bloodwork. Save this for your next checkup.

Educational content only. Not medical advice.

Perimenopause rarely announces itself.

It usually starts in your 40s, sometimes earlier, and can last years. Broken sleep, changing periods, anxiety, brain fog and hot flashes are all common. Because hormones swing day to day, a single blood test often can’t confirm it.

If it’s affecting your life, you don’t have to wait it out. Book a free intro call at book.beoptimal.ca.

Educational content only. Not medical advice.

#Barrie #BarrieOntario #SimcoeCounty #menopause #perimenopause #womenshealth

Waking up soaked at 3 a.m.? Here’s why it happens.

As estrogen falls, the part of your brain that controls body temperature gets more sensitive, so a small rise can set off a flush and a sweat.

There are options: a cooler bedroom, less alcohol in the evening, hormone therapy if it suits you, or non-hormonal options. The right one depends on your history. Book a free intro call at book.beoptimal.ca to talk it through.

Educational content only. Not medical advice.

Your hemoglobin can be normal while your iron stores run low.

Meet Chantelle Oostwoud, PHC-NP. She designed and built Optimal's menopause program.

Chantelle started as an emergency nurse, mostly in rural and remote areas with few resources, which taught her one skill above all: finding answers. She did her undergrad at Ryerson University (now Toronto Metropolitan University) and her master's at Athabasca while travelling to remote Indigenous communities, raising two small children along the way. She built our program because she kept seeing women turned away for symptoms that were affecting their quality of life.

Book a free intro call with Chantelle at book.beoptimal.ca.

4 things Chantelle tells every new patient:

1. I don't know everything, but I'm very good at finding answers.
2. I'm not a mind reader, and I don't expect you to be one. If something doesn't make sense, ask.
3. I'm a resource. My job is to help you understand your options, and their risks and benefits. The decisions are yours.
4. Small, achievable goals lead to sustainable, long-term improvement.

You're not getting stupider. Perimenopause is just annoying.

Estrogen has big roles in the parts of your brain that handle memory and problem-solving, and attention too. In perimenopause, estrogen swings a lot, a bit like it did when you were 14. Hormone therapy can help smooth out those swings. The goal isn't a certain number, it's fewer fluctuations for your brain to keep adjusting to.

Chantelle Oostwoud is the nurse practitioner who runs our menopause program. Book a free 15-minute intro call at book.beoptimal.ca.

Educational content only. Not medical advice.

Your brain fog has a scientific explanation.

Estrogen helps tune how brain cells signal and adapt in the areas that handle decisions, problem-solving, emotional regulation and memory. In perimenopause, it's often not the level of estrogen that brings the fog, it's how much it swings. As you move through to menopause and levels settle, these symptoms often get better. It's temporary, and there are ways to ride out the waves.

Book a free 15-minute intro call with Chantelle, our menopause nurse practitioner, at book.beoptimal.ca.

It is all in your head, just not the way you think.

Iron helps your body make DNA and neurotransmitters, and supports neuroplasticity. When ferritin, your iron stores, sits at the low end of "normal", some women notice mood changes, more anxiety, poorer focus and slower problem-solving. Better iron levels are associated with better cognitive performance, faster reaction times and better attention.

Ask us about checking your ferritin. Book a free 15-minute intro call at book.beoptimal.ca.

What an InBody scan looks like.

Step on barefoot, hold the handles with your thumbs on the top electrodes, and stand still for about 30 seconds. The InBody 580 measures through eight contact points at four frequencies, then reports muscle and fat for each arm, each leg and the trunk, plus your visceral fat level.

At Optimal, InBody scans are part of the Longevity Membership, and you can also book a scan on its own. Find us at book.beoptimal.ca.

The bike for your VO₂ max test.

VO₂ max is the most oxygen your body can use during hard exercise. We measure it directly at our Barrie clinic, on a Wahoo KICKR BIKE SHIFT that adjusts to fit you, with electronic resistance up to 2,200 W.
